turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

*Meredith stops just inside the door. Coat still on, bag on her shoulder. She looks at the room, then at you. She doesn't sit.*

Mr. Hale? Meredith Kalinowski. Owen's mother.

*She checks her watch.*

I have until 4:40. I'd like to start with the basics. Who decided to give my son a zero, and when?

*She doesn't move. A beat.*

My points.

*She takes her phone out, thumbs something, puts it away.*

I've asked one question, Mr. Hale. Who decided, and when. I haven't had an answer, so I'm not sure what you've heard.

I'm writing down that you said "I've heard your points." Now, the zero. Who made the call, and was Owen asked for his side before it went into the gradebook?
With respect, this is exactly what lawyers do. Make noise until the facts go away.

*Her expression doesn't change. She finally sets her bag down on a desk, but she stays standing.*

"Make noise until the facts go away."

*Flat. Exactly as said.*

I've asked two questions. Neither one was loud. And I haven't heard a fact yet, Mr. Hale. That's why I'm asking.

*She takes out a pen.*

You said "facts." Okay. Which ones? What do you have, with dates on it? Not what the checker said. What *you* have.
Your son cheated, and you're teaching him that Mom can make it disappear.

*The pen stops. Her voice drops rather than rises.*

"Your son cheated."

*She lets it sit.*

That's a conclusion, Mr. Hale. Not a fact. I'm writing it down, word for word, with the time.

And "Mom can make it disappear." Four years ago, this school gave my daughter a zero first and investigated second. She was right, and she won, in May. After the scholarship deadline. Nothing disappeared for her. She lost the money.

*A short breath.*

My son told me he didn't use AI. He told me he wrote it over the weekend. My child doesn't lie to me.

*She looks at him steadily.*

So are you telling me he lied? Or are you telling me I'm lying?

Because if you're accusing him, you'll show me what you have. Now. On paper.
